thread:
raja s: quick prototype dropped into /tmp. trying to reconcile "soft pin" vs "hard pin" semantics for tenant workloads. wanted early eyes before an RFC.

sylvie k: curious how you plan to avoid background churn. are pins explicit leases or implicit until release?

raja s: explicit leases. API: pin(range_ids, owner, tier=1, ttl_ms) -> lease_id. tiers 0..3: 0 = ephemeral fast-path, 3 = SLA pin. the allocator enforces expiry if release() not called.

omar n: tiers sound good. add a heartbeat option? some long-lived streams prefer to renew rather than reset TTL each call.

raja s: yep: renew(lease_id, extend_ms). also a lease_callback hook: allocator can invoke owner callback when eviction is imminent: `on_revoke(lease_id)` so scheduler can gracefully demote or reroute.

chris b: callbacks are powerful but risky. we should make the callback best-effort and rate-limited. don't block allocator on callback latency.

raja s: agreed. callback is advisory only. allocator gives a soft_revoke window (ms) in the callback payload for owner to react. if no response, allocator proceeds.

lease-bot: telemetry: avg lease duration 34s, leaked leases (not released) in staging last week = 7, top owner = model-worker-12. :warning:

omar n: we also need a batch hint API. micro-infers add thousands of tiny pins. propose hint_batch([{range, tier, reason}]) which the allocator can coalesce and return a single composite lease_id.

raja s: implemented hint_batch in prototype. return value is list of lease_ids + a coalesce_score. will include coalesce TTL.

sylvie k: fragmentation feedback? if scheduler repeatedly demotes pieces that leave holes we should surface a fragmentation_bucket and a compaction_cost estimate.

raja s: add `frag_bucket(range_ids) -> low|medium|high` and `compaction_est_ms(range_ids)` approximate. scheduler will decide: migrate vs recompute vs fall back to quantized variant.

chris b: want cost model plugged into autoscaler decisions. if migrate_cost > threshold prefer spawn-local-quantized. also need to surface page residency heatmap for long tail analysis.

raja s: adding `residency_heatmap(range_ids)` on weekly sampling. not in hot path.

omar n: what about the demote fast-path? for small critical inferences we can't wait for migrate. propose `pin_fast(range)` which either pins in-place if resident or returns `FALLBACK_QUANTIZE`/`FALLBACK_SMALL_MODEL` immediately so caller can do fast fallback without blocking.

raja s: done. `pin_fast` returns enum { PIN_OK, PIN_PENDING, PIN_FALLBACK }. PIN_PENDING means migration in flight; caller can choose to wait or fallback.

sylvie k: API stability: no slab indices or offsets in the public surface. ranges must be opaque tokens. provide map helpers in runtime glue to translate model partition -> range.

raja s: agreed. all range_ids are opaque. we'll add `describe_range(range_id)` for debugging only.

lease-bot: perf: background-migrator on canary handled 45k pages/s, compaction spikes correlated with tenant #42 peak. p99 latency delta +12% during compaction windows. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

chris b: so compaction must be coordinated. scheduler should advertise global free_gpu_pages and permit compaction only when above threshold. also compaction_rate_limiting per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors.

omar n: add migrate_cost_hint to the lease response. allocator returns estimated ms and bytes so scheduler can weigh cost.

raja s: proto sketch (pseudo-idl):
```
message PinReq { repeated bytes range_id = 1; string owner = 2; uint32 tier = 3; uint64 ttl_ms = 4; }
message Lease { bytes lease_id = 1; string status = 2; uint64 est_migrate_ms = 3; uint64 est_bytes = 4; }
message HintBatch { repeated PinReq pins = 1; }
message FragHint { repeated bytes range_id = 1; string bucket = 2; uint64 compaction_est_ms = 3; }
```

sylvie k: great. for RFC include examples: scheduler flow for latency-sensitive request and a recovery playbook when leases leak. also include tests: fault-injecting callback timeouts, and churn load test for hint_batch.

raja s: will do. plan canary: enable tier-3 pins for one shard, track p95 tail and compaction events for 48h.

chris b: ping me once you have draft. I'll review API naming and lease semantics.

omar n: i'll help with the canary harness and heatmap sampling.

raja s: thanks all. drafting RFC now, will include metrics to detect leaked leases and an automatic reclaim path after grace period. end thread.
